commands.path: create group apply
commands.summary: Plan and execute the create group reverse-ETL action
examples: pm service-now create group apply --plan <plan-name>
commands.risk: creates a new user group record; low-risk external mutation, no approval required
commands.approval: requires plan, preview, approval, and execute

commands.path: create incident apply
commands.summary: Plan and execute the create incident reverse-ETL action
examples: pm service-now create incident apply --plan <plan-name>
commands.risk: creates a new incident record; low-risk external mutation (a new ticket), no approval required
commands.approval: requires plan, preview, approval, and execute

commands.path: create user apply
commands.summary: Plan and execute the create user reverse-ETL action
examples: pm service-now create user apply --plan <plan-name>
commands.risk: creates a new ServiceNow user account record; a new user account granted whatever role/ACL defaults the instance applies is a higher-scrutiny mutation than an incident/group create
commands.approval: requires plan, preview, approval, and execute

commands.path: update group apply
commands.summary: Plan and execute the update group reverse-ETL action
examples: pm service-now update group apply --plan <plan-name>
commands.risk: mutates an existing group's recorded fields by sys_id, including active/manager; can change who is considered the group's membership owner
commands.approval: requires plan, preview, approval, and execute

commands.path: update incident apply
commands.summary: Plan and execute the update incident reverse-ETL action
examples: pm service-now update incident apply --plan <plan-name>
commands.risk: mutates an existing incident's recorded fields (only fields present in the submitted record are changed; ServiceNow's Table API PATCH/PUT both modify only the submitted fields, never the whole record) by sys_id
commands.approval: requires plan, preview, approval, and execute

commands.path: update user apply
commands.summary: Plan and execute the update user reverse-ETL action
examples: pm service-now update user apply --plan <plan-name>
commands.risk: mutates an existing user account's profile fields by sys_id, including active (deactivating a user's account revokes their instance access); higher-scrutiny than incident/group updates
commands.approval: requires plan, preview, approval, and execute
